# FSM_COS 0.1.0-alpha.7 — Internal Release Evidence Checklist

This is an internal checklist, not consumer documentation. It records required evidence, not a live status report. Always inspect the current `development` HEAD and its workflow runs; do not copy status, percentages, or artifact hashes from an older candidate.

## Candidate and source contract

Current candidate: the live `development` HEAD at the time of review. Record its full SHA in the release record after the candidate is frozen. Earlier green runs and artifact inspection belong to older commits and do not establish release readiness for the current HEAD.

- Confirm the intended source SHA and declared package version `0.1.0-alpha.7`.
- Review source, public API, tests, and consumer documentation together.
- Confirm every documented behavior is implemented and covered by relevant tests.
- Keep explicit limitations explicit; a staged metadata type is not proof of a complete staged-loading pipeline.
- Confirm the direct dependency set and versions against the project file and package artifact.

## Required CI and package evidence

- [ ] Pack/build/test, package verification, generated-visual checks, source integration, and public-NuGet compatibility all pass on the exact frozen `development` HEAD.
- [ ] CodeQL passes on that same exact SHA.
- [ ] Inspect the package artifact produced from that exact SHA: package ID/version, target framework, dependency metadata, license/readme, XML documentation, intended documentation/assets, and exclusions for maintainer notes.
- [ ] Confirm all packaged local Markdown links resolve within the package and SVG contract checks pass.
- [ ] Confirm the public-feed compatibility build uses the intended public dependency versions.
- [ ] Confirm `publish_nuget` remains skipped and no package was published.

Historical note: earlier candidate runs and an independently inspected `0.1.0-alpha.7` package were useful progress, but must not be marked as evidence for a later source SHA.

## Documentation and visual evidence

- [ ] Verify source and public contract guides agree on behavior, failure semantics, ownership, and limitations.
- [ ] Verify diagrams represent current contracts rather than future execution paths.
- [ ] Independently check SVG rendering and, where applicable, browser accessibility-tree exposure, keyboard interaction, and screen-reader behavior. Do not claim those checks passed without evidence.

## Alpha.7 scope boundary and explicit limitations

Alpha.7 ships a deliberately sequential composition path. Parallel loading is deferred and is **not** a release blocker.

The runtime path in this candidate validates the manifest, resolves dependency order, snapshots configuration, loads bundles sequentially, runs arbitration (bounded to ten rounds), and returns a runtime assembly. The runtime experience registry retains completed assemblies, supports lookup and explicit activation, and the runtime experience host can prepare/register an experience without automatically activating it. Duplicate runtime IDs are rejected.

This alpha does **not** claim repository localization or content-hash verification, bootstrap-only composition, background localization, live deferred promotion into an existing assembly, manifest refresh, atomic host handoff, generation leases/retirement, or serialize-then-relinquish shutdown. Collection snapshots protect collection structure, not the referenced domain-owned MicroBundle objects. Failures cannot automatically undo arbitrary external side effects; rollback is limited to the explicit MicroBundle rollback contract.

These are documented follow-on capabilities, not hidden blockers for the narrow Alpha.7 release. Do not describe deferred behavior as implemented.

## Deferred optimization: parallel loading

Parallel MicroBundle loading is intentionally out of scope for 0.1.0-alpha.7. Dependency-first sequential loading provides a straightforward completion contract: each load finishes before the next dependent load begins. Reconsider parallel loading only after the API defines how callers await complete load waves, how cancellation and partial failures are surfaced, how rollback coordinates with in-flight work, and benchmarks demonstrate a material benefit.

## Publication authorization is separate

- [ ] Obtain explicit owner authorization before publication.
- [ ] Verify the intended stable source commit and exact public-dependency artifact.
- [ ] Only then revisit the disabled publish guard and workflow dispatch path.
- [ ] After an authorized publication, verify the exact version on NuGet and record the source SHA, workflow run, and artifact hash.

Do not assign a readiness percentage from this checklist until each applicable gate has current evidence for the same candidate SHA.
